original_title: Three-dimensional finite element analysis of force systems generated by clear aligner attachments during upper canine retraction

authors.name: Lombardo L.
authors.affiliation: Department of Orthodontics, University of Ferrara, Ferrara, Italy

authors.name: Arreghini A.
authors.affiliation: Department of Orthodontics, University of Ferrara, Ferrara, Italy

authors.name: Siciliani G.
authors.affiliation: Department of Biomedical Engineering, Polytechnic University of Milan, Milan, Italy

abstract: Clear aligners have become a popular alternative to fixed appliances for orthodontic treatment. This study uses three-dimensional finite element analysis to evaluate force systems generated by seven attachment designs during upper canine retraction. The optimized root control attachment produced the most favorable moment-to-force ratio (10.2:1), while the rectangular attachment generated the highest absolute force (1.87 N). Attachment geometry critically determines the force system delivered to the tooth.
journal_or_origin: American Journal of Orthodontics and Dentofacial Orthopedics
reviewer_notes: Highly relevant to aligner product design. The FEA methodology is robust and the comparison of 7 attachment geometries provides actionable insights for optimizing attachment protocols.
executive_summary_en: This finite element analysis study compares seven clear aligner attachment designs for canine retraction, finding that optimized root control attachments produce the best moment-to-force ratios for bodily movement while rectangular attachments generate the highest forces. Key insight for product development: attachment geometry is the primary determinant of biomechanical performance.
executive_summary_es: Este estudio de analisis de elementos finitos compara siete disenos de ataches para alineadores transparentes en la retraccion canina, encontrando que los ataches optimizados para control radicular producen las mejores relaciones momento-fuerza para movimiento en masa. Hallazgo clave: la geometria del atache es el principal determinante del rendimiento biomecanico.

original_title: Artificial intelligence-driven treatment planning in orthodontics: a convolutional neural network approach for predicting extraction decisions and anchorage requirements

authors.name: Chen W.
authors.affiliation: Department of Orthodontics, Peking University School of Stomatology, Beijing, China

authors.name: Park J.H.
authors.affiliation: Postgraduate Orthodontic Program, Arizona School of Dentistry and Oral Health, A.T. Still University, Mesa, AZ, USA

abstract: This study develops and validates a deep learning model for predicting orthodontic extraction decisions and anchorage requirements from pretreatment records. The CNN achieved 93.2% accuracy for extraction classification (AUC = 0.967) and 87.4% for anchorage prediction. Model-panel agreement (kappa = 0.81) exceeded inter-rater agreement among orthodontists (kappa = 0.78).
executive_summary_en: A multi-input CNN achieves 93.2% accuracy in predicting orthodontic extraction decisions from cephalometric radiographs and digital models, with model-clinician agreement surpassing inter-rater reliability among orthodontists. This represents a significant step toward AI-assisted treatment planning that could be integrated into clinical decision support workflows.
executive_summary_es: Una CNN multi-entrada alcanza el 93.2% de precision en la prediccion de decisiones de extraccion ortodontica a partir de radiografias cefalometricas y modelos digitales, con una concordancia modelo-clinico que supera la fiabilidad entre evaluadores. Representa un avance significativo hacia la planificacion de tratamiento asistida por IA.

original_title: Clear Aligners Versus Fixed Braces for the Treatment of Class II Division 1 Malocclusion in Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial

authors.name: Hediger S.
authors.affiliation: University of Zurich, Center of Dental Medicine

abstract: This multicenter RCT compares treatment efficacy, duration, and patient-reported outcomes of thermoplastic clear aligners versus conventional fixed orthodontic appliances in adult patients with Class II Division 1 malocclusion. Primary outcome is PAR index reduction. Secondary outcomes include treatment duration, OHIP-14 scores, and 3D digital model superimposition analysis of tooth movement accuracy.
reviewer_notes: Critical trial for competitive positioning. Multicenter design with robust methodology. Should monitor for interim results and final publication. Direct comparison with our product category.
executive_summary_en: A multicenter RCT (n=120) at three European universities comparing Invisalign Comprehensive vs. Damon Q2 self-ligating brackets for Class II Division 1 correction. Currently recruiting with estimated completion in 2027. This trial will provide high-quality evidence on clear aligner efficacy for a specific malocclusion type, with direct implications for product positioning and clinical guidelines.
executive_summary_es: Ensayo clinico aleatorizado multicentrico (n=120) en tres universidades europeas que compara Invisalign Comprehensive vs. brackets autoligables Damon Q2 para correccion de Clase II Division 1. Actualmente reclutando, con finalizacion estimada en 2027. Proporcionara evidencia de alta calidad sobre la eficacia de alineadores para este tipo de maloclusion.

original_title: DentalSeg: A Multi-Scale Transformer-Based Architecture for Precise Dental Structure Segmentation in Panoramic Radiographs

authors.name: Zhang Y.
authors.affiliation: Department of Computer Science, Stanford University

authors.name: Rodriguez-Garcia M.
authors.affiliation: Artificial Intelligence Research Lab, Technical University of Munich

abstract: We propose DentalSeg, a novel multi-scale transformer-based architecture for dental structure segmentation in panoramic radiographs. The model incorporates tooth-aware positional encoding and achieves a mean Dice score of 0.947 for individual tooth segmentation and 0.891 for pathology detection across three public datasets totaling 4,218 radiographs, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by 2.1-4.8 percentage points.
executive_summary_en: DentalSeg introduces a transformer-based architecture achieving state-of-the-art dental structure segmentation (Dice 0.947) in panoramic radiographs. The tooth-aware positional encoding is a novel contribution. Potential application in automated treatment planning pipelines and quality assurance for aligner manufacturing from panoramic X-rays.
executive_summary_es: DentalSeg introduce una arquitectura basada en transformers que alcanza segmentacion de estructuras dentales de vanguardia (Dice 0.947) en radiografias panoramicas. La codificacion posicional consciente del diente es una contribucion novedosa. Potencial aplicacion en pipelines de planificacion de tratamiento automatizada.

original_title: Align Technology's ClinCheck AI: patent analysis reveals next-generation treatment outcome prediction using multimodal generative models

authors.name: Align Technology Inc.
authors.affiliation: Align Technology, San Jose, CA, USA

abstract: Patent application US20240189142A1 describes a system and method for predicting orthodontic treatment outcomes using multimodal generative AI models. The invention combines 3D intraoral scan data, 2D radiographic images, and patient demographic/clinical features to generate predicted post-treatment dentition states. Key innovations include a diffusion model for 3D tooth position prediction, a physics-informed neural network for simulating tissue response, and a reinforcement learning agent for optimizing staging sequences. The patent also covers integration with cloud-based treatment planning platforms and real-time clinician feedback loops.
reviewer_notes: HIGH PRIORITY: Align Technology patent reveals significant investment in generative AI for treatment outcome prediction. The diffusion model approach for 3D tooth position prediction and physics-informed neural networks for tissue simulation represent a potential competitive threat. Recommend immediate strategic review and assessment of our own AI roadmap alignment.
executive_summary_en: Align Technology has filed a patent describing a next-generation AI system for orthodontic treatment outcome prediction combining diffusion models for 3D tooth positioning, physics-informed neural networks for tissue simulation, and RL-based staging optimization. This represents a significant competitive signal indicating Align's heavy investment in generative AI. The system integrates with cloud platforms and includes clinician feedback loops, suggesting a move toward fully automated treatment planning.
executive_summary_es: Align Technology ha presentado una patente describiendo un sistema de IA de nueva generacion para prediccion de resultados de tratamiento ortodontico que combina modelos de difusion para posicionamiento dental 3D, redes neuronales informadas por fisica para simulacion de tejidos, y optimizacion de staging basada en RL. Representa una senal competitiva significativa que indica la fuerte inversion de Align en IA generativa.
